clue.text: At fault over a net repair

indicators.note: something at fault has gone wrong, so the letters that follow are out of their proper order

blocks.note: the three words supply the eight letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has damaged a net and must now repair it.
explanation.definitionFit: To renovate is to restore something to good condition, a synonym of repair as a verb.

clue.text: Quietly conducts appeals

blocks.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
to conduct a group is to lead it

explanation.surface: A conductor who makes requests in a soft voice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conducts' suggests an orchestra, which fits the musical P, but here it simply means guides.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead is to make an earnest request, so pleads matches the verb appeals.

clue.text: Note: often it may be seen at a wedding

definitions.text: Note: often it may be seen at a wedding

indicators.note: may be suggests the letters could become something else when arranged differently

blocks.note: C is one of the musical notes
taken as written, as letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A remark that something is commonly spotted at weddings.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the description: the note plus 'often it', rearranged, gives the paper scattered over newly-weds.
explanation.definitionFit: Confetti, small pieces of coloured paper, is thrown over a bride and groom, so it is often seen at a wedding.

clue.text: Prophet has spoken about key to ecstasy

indicators.note: the spoken word goes round the next piece, sitting about it
the key to a word is its opening letter, which unlocks it

blocks.note: oral means spoken rather than written
c (circa) means about, as in a date
the first letter of ecstasy

explanation.surface: A seer has been talking about the secret of rapture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' does double work: C (circa) sits inside the word for spoken, then E follows.
explanation.definitionFit: An oracle is a person through whom a god speaks, so a prophet or seer.

clue.text: Insect the French found on vegetable

blocks.note: beet is a root vegetable
le is French for the

explanation.surface: A bug discovered sitting on a vegetable in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found on' places the French word after the vegetable, as in an across answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A beetle is an insect with hard wing cases, a common example of the class.

clue.text: Beer-maker uses brown jug

blocks.note: br is a standard abbreviation for brown
a ewer is a large jug

explanation.surface: A brewer serves his ale from a brown jug.
explanation.definitionFit: A brewer is a person or firm that brews beer, so a beer-maker.

clue.text: Old Royal Free Hospital previously used to be dreadful

indicators.note: previously says the last-named piece comes earlier, so it is placed at the front

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital
O is the abbreviation for old
R is the abbreviation for royal, as in RN
to free someone of something is to rid them of it

explanation.surface: A London hospital, the Royal Free, was once a dreadful place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Previously' puts the hospital's letter in front of the others. The Royal Free is a real London hospital, which disguises the separate abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Horrid is an informal synonym of dreadful, meaning very unpleasant.

clue.text: Gloomy auditor found in dull surroundings

indicators.note: something found in a place is enclosed by it, so one piece sits inside the other
surroundings are what lie all round, so the word before it wraps the other piece

blocks.note: dry can mean dull and uninteresting
an auditor is a listener, and the ear is what listens

explanation.surface: A miserable accountant sits in drab surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Auditor' looks like an accountant, but here it means a hearer, hence the organ of hearing.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary means dull and depressing, a close synonym of gloomy.

clue.text: Archers get a character reshuffle when uninvited guest makes an appearance

indicators.note: a reshuffle of characters means the letters themselves are moved into a new order

blocks.note: the three words supply the eleven letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The Archers, a long-running BBC radio soap, shakes up its cast when a newcomer turns up unannounced.
explanation.walkthrough: The Archers is a BBC radio soap opera, so 'character reshuffle' reads as a cast change.
explanation.definitionFit: A gatecrasher attends a party or event without an invitation.

clue.text: Fellow trotted over with a hat

indicators.note: over suggests turning something round, so the word reads backwards

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow
a horse that trotted was ridden; to trot is to ride at that pace
taken as written

explanation.surface: A man trotted across wearing a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt hat with a creased crown, an example of a hat.

clue.text: A Freddie Flintoff England century initially has Mr Dexter emotional

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the preceding words

blocks.note: the first letters of these five words
Ted Dexter was a former England cricket captain

explanation.surface: A cricket scene: a Flintoff century for England moves Dexter.
explanation.walkthrough: Freddie Flintoff and Ted Dexter are both England cricketers; Dexter's first name is needed, not his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: Being affected means being moved or touched emotionally, so it fits emotional.

clue.text: Rave about girl

indicators.note: about suggests moving things around, so the letters are put in a fresh order

blocks.note: the four letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone enthuses wildly about a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Vera is a female name; in crosswords a girl often stands for any girl's name.

clue.text: Reheat stew cooked for lover

indicators.note: cooking transforms ingredients, so the letters are mixed into a new form

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Warming up a casserole for one's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetheart is a person one loves, a term of endearment for a lover.

clue.text: Leaf catcher solves problem about locomotive

indicators.note: the puzzle word wraps about the next piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: a teaser is a tricky problem or puzzle
a locomotive pulls a train, standing for it

explanation.surface: Something that catches leaves cracks a railway puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaf' means tea leaves, not those from trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A tea strainer is placed over a cup to catch loose tea leaves as the tea is poured.

clue.text: Photos taken under the influence of strong drink?

blocks.note: surface reading: pictures snapped by someone drunk
setter's reading: a slurring drinker says the word for photos with a sh sound, giving a German spirit

explanation.surface: Pictures shot by a photographer who has had too much.
explanation.walkthrough: Say the casual word for photos the way a drunk might slur it, and you get the name of a strong spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: Schnapps is a strong alcoholic spirit, typically distilled from fruit or grain.

clue.text: Leave out climbing nonsense! Take the lift!

indicators.note: out suggests something put out of place, so the letters are disordered
in a down answer climbing means read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the five letters to be rearranged
rot is nonsense, rubbish

explanation.surface: Stop that silly climbing and use the lift instead!
explanation.definitionFit: Elevator is the American word for a lift carrying people between floors.

clue.text: Child's toy can kind of rock

blocks.note: first meaning: a small glass ball used in children's games
second meaning: a crystalline limestone used in sculpture

explanation.surface: A toy that can also be made of stone.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a small glass ball children play with and a metamorphic stone prized for statues.

clue.text: Jaguar, for example, needs large catalytic converter

blocks.note: big means large
cat is the everyday short name for a catalytic converter

explanation.surface: A Jaguar car needs a large exhaust part.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaguar looks like the car, which suits the converter, but it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The jaguar is one of the large wild felines, alongside lions and tigers, an example of the group.

clue.text: Wash my kilt out with pure spirit

indicators.note: washed out, the letters lose their order and come back rearranged

blocks.note: the ten letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Cleaning a Scotsman's kilt with neat spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Malt whisky is made from malted barley alone, sold as an unblended spirit.

clue.text: Temperature at which, allegedly, convulsion occurs

indicators.note: allegedly means as it is said, pointing to how the word is spoken

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature
which and witch are pronounced the same

explanation.surface: A medical note about the temperature at which a fit happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A twitch is a sudden involuntary jerk of a muscle, a small spasm.

clue.text: He agrees with everything men say when drunk

indicators.note: a drunk staggers about, so the letters reel into a different order

blocks.note: the six letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A man who goes along with whatever drunk men say.
explanation.definitionFit: A yes-man is a sycophant who always agrees with superiors, the person described.

clue.text: Long poem is illustrated with some exquisite pictures

indicators.note: with some means only part of the following words is used, the letters lying inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: A lengthy poem decorated with fine artwork.
explanation.definitionFit: An epic is a long narrative poem about heroic deeds, such as the Iliad.

clue.text: Resign over police being in decline

indicators.note: over suggests turning something round, so the word is read backwards
being in means placed inside, so one piece is put within the other

blocks.note: to abate is to decline or lessen
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the UK plain-clothes police

explanation.surface: A police chief steps down as the force falls into decline.
explanation.walkthrough: The CID is the detective branch of British police forces.
explanation.definitionFit: To abdicate is to give up a throne or office, so to resign.

clue.text: Few would deface church

blocks.note: to scar something is to mark or deface it
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Only a few would vandalise a church.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarce means in short supply, so things that are scarce are few.

clue.text: He's first off at cracking pace to avoid capture

indicators.note: first off means the opening letter is removed
something cracking breaks apart, so the letters are scattered and re-formed

blocks.note: taken as written, before its first letter goes
the four letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A runner leads at a cracking pace to get away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cracking pace' reads as a fast speed, but cracking is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To escape is to get free, so it means to avoid being caught.

clue.text: Unusual exit

blocks.note: first meaning: an informal adjective for strange or unconventional
second meaning: the way to leave a place

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for bizarre and also the sign marking a door to leave by.
